secret.label: Forged identity
secret.description: Rosenbaum is not the person the papers say. Nothing about the evening is hidden; the lie is all in the paperwork.

motive.description: was about to be exposed by the victim

people.name: Wendell Cheatham
people.relationshipToVictim: the victim’s neighbour across the airshaft

secret.label: Blackmailing the victim
secret.description: Cheatham meets the victim alone at the office from 7:00 PM and asks for money.

secret.label: Fencing stolen goods
secret.description: Vogel hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at Mancuso’s from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM.

secret.label: Organizing the shop
secret.description: Hauck is at the ferry slip from 10:30 PM to 11:00 PM signing men up, which is a firing offence and worse.

motive.description: blamed the victim for a ruin

people.name: Carmine Alfano
people.role: a doorman at a club with no sign on it

secret.label: Gambling debt
secret.description: Alfano slips off to Mancuso’s from 8:00 PM to 8:30 PM to settle with a bookmaker.

secret.label: Murder
secret.description: Brauer is at the suite from 8:00 PM, alone with Hurwitz when it happens at 8:00 PM.

coverSecret.label: Blackmailing the victim

motive.description: wanted the victim out of a lease

method.name: strangling with a cord
method.bodyEvidence: A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.

traces.description: the regular was drinking sherry, and said twice what he thought of the beer

anchors.timing: while the milk wagon was in the street

anchors.sceneFact: The rain came on at {T}. It got in at the window, and the wet had stopped spreading by the time the body was found.

Hurwitz was found at the suite. His watch glass broke against the floor and the hands have not moved since. The milk wagon was at the corner at 8:00 PM, where the driver’s round puts him every night.
The coroner puts death between 7:00 PM and 8:30 PM — two hours of nothing useful. A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.
A length of sash cord is gone from the third floor. A cut end of the same hemp is still tied to the fitting it was taken from.
Hauck puts Hurwitz at the Wyckoff when the regular came in for his seat, which was 7:30 PM, and alive enough to argue about the weather.
Kessler puts Hurwitz at the Wyckoff when the regular came in for his seat, which was 7:30 PM, and alive enough to argue about the weather.

Vogel says Hurwitz told Rosenbaum that the story would run whether Rosenbaum liked it or not.
Found at the suite: A clipping about the failure of Hauck’s business, with Hurwitz’s name underlined twice in pencil.
Kreuzer says Hauck said Hurwitz had taken everything and would be made to feel it.
Found at the office: A lease assignment made out in Brauer’s name, waiting only on Hurwitz’s signature.
Prentiss says Hurwitz told Brauer the lease would go to somebody else at the quarter day.
Cheatham hired us, and wants it known that Brauer wanted the victim out of a lease, and would rather we started there.
Prentiss on Rosenbaum: Rosenbaum’s registration card gives an address on a street that does not exist.
Vogel on Rosenbaum: Two signatures of Rosenbaum’s, a month apart, are in different hands.
Alfano on Rosenbaum: Rosenbaum answers to the name a half-second late, every time.
A union card in Rosenbaum’s coat lining carries a different surname and a 1919 date.
A steamship ticket stub among Rosenbaum’s things, in the name of a man who died at Belleau Wood.
The name Rosenbaum was born with turns up on a desertion warrant from 1918. Rosenbaum has been hiding from the Army for eleven years and from nobody else.
The papers are forged and the reason is plain: Rosenbaum was put out of the country once already and does not mean to be put out twice.
Kreuzer on Cheatham: Cheatham and the victim were heard at the office, and one of them was doing all the talking.
Rosenbaum on Cheatham: Cheatham has come into money lately and has no visible way of having come into money.
Hauck on Cheatham: The victim had been drawing cash in amounts that did not match anything in the accounts.
An envelope at the office with nothing in it, addressed in the victim’s hand to no one.
A photograph at the office, folded small, of something the victim would have paid to keep folded.
The victim’s bank book settles it: four payments, and Cheatham at the office from 7:00 PM collecting the fifth. It is extortion, and an extortionist wants the man alive.
The thing Cheatham was holding over the victim turns up, and it was worth more to Cheatham every month than once.
Prentiss on Vogel: Vogel was carrying a parcel into Mancuso’s and came out without it.
Cheatham on Vogel: There is a man who meets people at Mancuso’s and nobody will say his name out loud.
Kessler on Vogel: Vogel has been selling things that were never Vogel’s to sell.
Wrapping paper and a cut string at Mancuso’s, and the shop it came from closed two years ago.
A pawn ticket at Mancuso’s in a name that does not exist, made out at the hour in question.
The receiver at Mancuso’s would rather talk than be held: Vogel was there from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM handing over a parcel of somebody else’s silver, which is a charge Vogel will take over this one.
The goods turn up, tagged and dated, and the tag puts Vogel at Mancuso’s from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM with both hands full.
Brauer on Hauck: Hauck has been seen with men from three different shops and none of them were drinking.
Kreuzer on Hauck: There is a list going round and Hauck’s name is at the top of it.
Rosenbaum on Hauck: A private agency has had a man on Hauck for a fortnight.
A sheaf of signed cards at the ferry slip, forty of them, in a strapped envelope.
A hall rental receipt at the ferry slip made out to a name that means nothing to anyone.
Forty men will swear to it if they have to: Hauck was at the ferry slip from 10:30 PM to 11:00 PM taking their names, and the only thing Hauck is guilty of is a charter.
The agency’s own operative confirms it. He was watching Hauck at the ferry slip for the whole of it, from 10:30 PM to 11:00 PM, and wrote it up for his employer.
Cheatham on Alfano: Alfano was asking around for a hundred dollars in a hurry earlier in the week.
Kessler on Alfano: A man nobody knew was waiting for Alfano at Mancuso’s and would not give a name.
Prentiss on Alfano: Alfano goes very quiet when the racing wire is mentioned.
Betting slips at Mancuso’s in Alfano’s pocketbook, all of them losers, all of them this month.
A book of markers at Mancuso’s with Alfano’s initials against four of them.
The bookmaker’s runner is found and will say it: Alfano was at Mancuso’s from 8:00 PM to 8:30 PM paying off eleven hundred dollars, a dollar at a time, and went nowhere near the killing.
The book at Mancuso’s has the payment entered against Alfano’s name and the time beside it, from 8:00 PM to 8:30 PM, in the clerk’s own hand.
